title: 1000 Layer Networks for Self-Supervised RL: Scaling Depth Can Enable New G

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper states: “the parameter count scales linearly with width but quadratically with depth.” For the described fixed-width residual MLPs, this is backwards: each dense layer has O(w^2) parameters, so parameter count is approximately linear in depth and quadratic in width. Appendix B.6 correctly states the opposite (“Both FLOPs and memory grow more rapidly with width than with depth, as they scale quadratically with width but only linearly with depth”), creating a direct internal contradiction.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.5, Figure 9 and Section 3 definition of the CRL critic
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Section 3 defines the critic as a dot-product score, f(s,a,g)=phi(s,a)^T psi(g), and trains the actor to maximize that score. Figure 9 instead states that its “Q values” are Q(s,a,g)=||phi(s,a)-psi(g)||_2. Maximizing the stated positive L2 distance would favor embeddings farther from the goal, not goal reaching. No negative sign, inverse distance, or separate energy-to-Q conversion is supplied. Thus Figure 9's claimed Q-function visualization is inconsistent with both the stated method and optimization direction.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction contribution bullet and Figure 1 caption
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The introduction claims “more than 20× in half of the environments,” but Table 1 has only four of ten tasks strictly above 20×: Ant U5-Maze (50×), Humanoid (42×), Humanoid U-Maze (40×), and Humanoid Big Maze (600×). Ant U4-Maze is reported as exactly 20×, not more than 20×. Therefore the stated “half” and “more than 20×” summary is not supported by the paper's own table.

Reported performance values for what are presented as the same Scaled CRL depth experiments conflict substantially without an explanation of a different protocol or statistic. For example, Table 1 reports Humanoid depth 4/64 as 12.6/530 and Arm Push Easy as 308/620, whereas Figure 13 reports 19.5/756 and 308/762, respectively. Ant Big Maze is likewise 61/420 in Table 1 versus 60.7/441 in Figure 13. Section 4.1 says single-number performance is the average of the final five epochs, but Figure 13 does not identify a different measurement. These incompatible numerical summaries need reconciliation.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.2, Section 4.4 (“Training Contrastive RL with 1000+ Layers”), Appendix A.1, and Figure 12 references
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: “Figure 12” is used for incompatible content. Section 4.2 says Figure 12 compares methods against SAC, HER variants, GCBC, and GCSL; Appendix A.1 indeed labels its baseline-comparison figure as Figure 12. But Section 4.4 says the results for 256/1024-layer Humanoid experiments are “shown in Figure 12,” and the nearby caption for the deep Humanoid plots is also labeled Figure 12. One figure number cannot identify both distinct experiments, so the cross-references do not permit a reader to verify the claims.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 4.4, “Deep Networks Unlock Batch Size Scaling”
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The subsection title and Figure 7 caption assert that deep networks “unlock batch size scaling” and can use larger batches “to achieve further improvements.” The immediately following interpretive paragraph reaches the opposite conclusion: Figure 7 shows “only marginal or inconsistent improvements” and “the overall benefit of batch size scaling remains uncertain.” The positive headline/caption is not supported by the stated result and should be corrected or qualified.

predicted_errors.error_location: Figure 1 caption, Introduction contribution bullet, and Section 4.3
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The Figure 1 caption says critical-depth jumps “correspond to the emergence of qualitatively distinct policies,” and the introduction says gains “correspond to qualitatively distinct policies that emerge with scale.” Yet Section 4.3 concedes: “we do not find conclusive quantitative evidence that these behaviors represent consistent qualitative leaps” and describes the observations as anecdotal and unstable. The stronger headline claims overstate the evidence acknowledged in the body.

The two tables give incompatible wall-clock times for ostensibly the same Humanoid U-Maze depth runs: Table 3 reports 8.72 h at depth 4 and 46.74 h at depth 64, while Table 4 reports 3.23 h and 17.33 h, respectively. Table 4 is described as training “from Depth 4 up to Depth 1024 in the Humanoid U-Maze environment,” but does not specify a different training horizon, hardware allocation, batch size, or protocol that would explain the 2.5–2.7× discrepancy. This prevents reproducibility and makes the wall-clock conclusions incomparable.

The text calls SAC “the strongest baseline” and bases the wall-clock comparison exclusively on surpassing SAC's final score. The paper's own Figure 13 shows cases where SAC is not the best listed baseline: on Humanoid, SAC+HER is 356 versus SAC's 330, and on Arm Push Easy SAC+HER is 423 versus SAC's 422. Selecting SAC as the universal threshold therefore does not establish superiority over the strongest baseline and biases the claimed 7/10 wall-clock result.

predicted_errors.error_location: Sections 4.1–4.6, Tables 1–6, and Appendix B hyperparameters
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper reports many means with “±” values and makes claims about critical thresholds, 2–600× gains, and baseline superiority, but never states the number of independent random seeds, whether “±” is a standard deviation, standard error, or confidence interval, or how seeds were paired across depths/baselines. The claimed final-score statistic is only described as an average over five epochs, which is not a substitute for independent-run uncertainty. This omission makes statistical reliability and the alleged discontinuous depth effects impossible to assess.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, paragraph describing reward-free self-supervised RL, citation to Lee et al. (2022)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The sentence claims that cited work demonstrates systems that “explore and learn policies without reference to a reward function or demonstrations,” citing “Eysenbach et al., 2021, 2022; Lee et al., 2022.” The listed Lee et al. (2022) reference is “Multi-Game Decision Transformers,” an offline decision-transformer work trained on game trajectory data and reward/return conditioning; it is not a reward-free, no-demonstration online self-supervised goal-reaching method. This citation does not support the attributed claim.
